designs.units_and_screens:
UNITS. ICA-192 logcosh and ICA-192 skew on D3 block A: 384 directions. Logcosh/skew pairs with |cos| >= 0.8 are twins and are counted as one family (e64 section 5).

SCREENS (frozen before any label):
- (a) eta2(token) of y <= 0.30.
- (b) eta2(token) of y^2 <= 0.30.
- (c) Split-half |cos|, the smaller of the even and odd halves in the same D3 basis, >= 0.80. The floor comes from the grid {0.80, 0.70} on P3: 0.80 unless the recovering P3 control unit falls below it. Chance is the p99.9 of the best match for 10,000 random directions in 192 dims, reported (about 0.35 expected).
- (d) Tail diversity (new), on the heavy-tail 1% (about 4,060 rows on D3): >= 200 documents, >= 50 token types, largest type share <= 0.30, and largest single-document share <= 0.02.
  - On D2 (2,034 tail rows; the D2-equivalent document cap is 0.04), 181/192 units pass, all 11 failures on type share.
  - The controls pass with margin: #146 has 654 documents, 788 types, type share 0.059 and document share 0.012; #128 has 384, 596, 0.059 and 0.019.
- Bimodality is off.

OTHER D2 FEASIBILITY NUMBERS (one half only). Split-half median 0.73; 82/192 units >= 0.8; control units 0.88-0.93. eta2(y^2) max 0.26. Median excess kurtosis 3.1, with 172/192 units > 1.

NAMING (label phase, mechanical, in order):
1. The e64 extended battery under the section 6.1 rule: |AUROC| >= 0.75, or a 1% tail >= 3x the base rate and >= 0.10; graded features |rho| >= 0.5. On D2 the v1 battery alone names 64/192 block units, mostly through after_digit (29), next_continuation (13) and next_newline (12).
2. The 16 e64c rules, scored on an en_core_web_trf parse of D3, at |AUROC| >= 0.65.
3. Next-token category rules (the e66 categories: preposition, subordinator, temporal, punctuation, newline, digit, capitalised) at |AUROC| >= 0.65. These name the confirmed-but-covered L12 adjunct family and its relatives.
4. TOP64-SHADOW: u's heavy-tail-1% indicator is ranked at |AUROC| >= 0.75 by some single D3 top-64 reference unit, or u's heavy tail overlaps that unit's two-sided 2% tail at >= 0.25. On D2, 22/192 units reach 0.75.
5. V2-SHADOW: |cos| >= 0.5 between u's raw-space pattern and any of the 78 screened frozen e64 L12 directions (e64_maps_L12.npz).
6. Analyst context reading, only for units that survive 1-5, under the e64 section 6.2 standard (>= 8 of 12 contexts share one specific construction). It is sealed before S3.

CANDIDATES = screened and unnamed by 1-6. On D2, 97/192 logcosh units are battery-unnamed with readability < 0.70, and about 43% pass the repro screen. Expect about 30-60 candidates across both contrasts before S3, R3 and coverage.

REPORTED FOR EVERY UNIT:
- tail-TDI and the identity-suspect flag;
- the SAE-error share of the score: the variance of the score computed from h - SAE(h) (L12 16k big), divided by the score's variance. On D2, block units sit at 0.29-0.35 and top-64 units at 0.12-0.19;
- energy in the boundary bands (components 65-80 and 241-256);
- seed stability (a seed-3 refit);
- max |cos| to the e64 L12 directions.
designs.behavioural_tier:
The e65 rig is reused unchanged except for the subspace of the RAND bank and the site source. Model in bf16, eager attention, MPS; the push is applied at the site position only.

DOSE. c*sigma_d with c in {0.5, 1, 2, 4}, gate at c* = 2. Sign consistency (the share of the 20 commonest site token types with mean Delta > 0) must be >= 0.8 at some c <= 2. sigma_d is the raw SD of the unsteered projection at prompt positions >= 4.
- bf16 is adequate for block directions. Block-A SDs are about 27-42 even after identity removal, so a 2-sigma push is about 0.06*sigma_d per coordinate, well above bf16's half-ulp at the kept coordinates (median |h| 16, p99 107).
- e66 measured a realised dose of 0.999-1.000 at L12.
- A unit whose realised dose at c* is < 0.9 is "dose-void" and gets no verdict.

READOUT. Delta = [lse(logits[T_u]) - lse(logits[R_u])] steered minus unsteered. T_u is the blind signature from the next tokens of D3's heavy-tail 1% (e64.signature). R_u is frequency-matched (+-10% corpus count, seed 6400 + L order as e65).

TWO RAND BANKS ON B5:
- (i) For the rig anchor: 99 directions pulled back from e64's 64-d L12 subspace (P_U, P_sd from e64_maps_L12.npz), as in e65, with fresh seed 6810 + L.
- (ii) For block units: 99 directions g ~ N(0, I_192) in D3 block-A whitened coordinates, pulled back with U_A diag(sd_A) g, embedded with 1038 = 0, normalised, each dosed by its own sigma.
Neither bank is orthogonalised; the max |cos| to each unit is reported.

SIG. u's push is scored with every other screened block-A unit's signature (twin excluded, T_u tokens removed, v used only if >= 5 tokens remain).

PASS = Delta_uu(c*) > 0, sign consistency, Delta > the RAND max, and Delta > the SIG max.

ORDER ON B5:
1. Rig-continuity anchor: the frozen e64 L12 logcosh #33 (quote) with its e64 signature, against bank (i). If it fails, STOP behaviour: the rig or the site source is broken.
2. Block anchor: D3's recovered quote unit, or the paren unit if quote was not recovered (paren failed at L12 in e65; quote passed three times), against bank (ii). If it fails: "no behavioural verdict in block A".
3. Supervised block anchor, NON-GATING: the P3 quote probe direction restricted to block A and pulled back, at all four doses. It separates "block directions carry no causal weight" from "the ICA control unit is too weak".
4. Only if steps 1 and 2 pass: every candidate surviving G2-G5, at all four doses.

B6. The block anchor and every B5 pass, on fresh sites, with fresh sigma and a fresh block-A bank (seed 6910 + L). If the B6 anchor fails, no B6 verdict is issued.

C3 (pre-registered now, e66 style). One primary test per surviving family, the logcosh member first; the block anchor goes first; CONFIRMED iff the primary passes the same rule. Per-test bound 0.010; expected false confirmations <= 0.01 x the number of families.

Named non-candidate units are not steered: the sibling rank is dropped to save time.
designs.coverage_check:
This is e67's rubric adapted to block directions. It runs on every R3-replicated candidate BEFORE steering (G5), and again in full (including Neuronpedia lookups for the L13 resid_post dictionaries) on any C3-confirmed family.

DICTIONARIES (already on disk): resid_post_all 16k l0_big and l0_small at L10, L11, L12, L13 and L14; resid_post L13 65k l0_big, 16k l0_medium and 65k l0_medium. The 262k dictionaries are used only if the user approves a re-download and the folder stays under 18 GB after the activation caches are deleted.

COVERED iff a single latent meets both conditions:
- either decoder |cos| >= 0.7 with d_u AND above the block-subspace null p99.9 (1,000 random block-A pullbacks; the isotropic null is reported too), or activation |r| >= 0.7 with u's D3 score;
- AND that latent passes a behavioural match: among its 200 strongest D3 rows, the next-token-in-T_u rate is >= 0.8x the unit's own heavy-tail rate and >= 2x the base rate; or >= 25% of those rows lie in u's heavy 1% tail.
PARTIALLY COVERED iff <= 5 signed-OMP decoder rows reach cos 0.9. NOT COVERED otherwise.

ALSO REPORTED:
- atoms needed for cos 0.8 and 0.9 (signed and non-negative OMP), against the null median;
- the best activation |r|;
- the SAE-error share of the unit's score for every dictionary at L12 and L13. A unit with error share >= 0.5 is labelled "SAE-dark"; on D2 no block unit got there (max 0.35).

Activations are computed from D3's stored raw rows with the dictionaries' own fp32 JumpReLU encode, in float32 throughout (the e67b lesson).
designs.falsifiers_and_stop_rules:
F0. P3: no control recovered on any rung of the ladder -> STOP before D3. "Block A is not searchable at L12"; the probe ceilings and the planted detection limit are reported.
F1. D3: no control recovered -> STOP before labels.
F2. Shadow self-test fails -> switch to the 0.70 readability fallback and report it (not a stop).
F3. S3 yield gate fails -> STOP before R3 and behaviour: "the unnamed ICA structure beyond PC 64 is mostly what ICA also finds in word salad".
F4. No control replicates on R3 -> the replication tier is uninformative and no discovery is claimed.
F5. All replicated candidates are COVERED -> "beyond-top-64 structure exists but Gemma Scope 2 already has it" (the goal's negative answer); no behaviour is run.
F6. The rig-continuity anchor fails on B5 -> STOP behaviour (rig or site source broken).
F7. The block anchor fails on B5 -> "no behavioural verdict in block A"; the outcome is capped at "replicated, uncovered geometric lead". The supervised anchor's result says whether block directions lack causal weight or only the ICA unit is weak.
F8. B5 candidate passes <= the sum of the per-unit bounds -> none counted.
F9. No B5 pass survives B6, or no family is confirmed on C3 -> verdict: "no uncovered, unnamed occurrence variable in raw L12 PCs 65-256 found by this instrument". This is quoted with the planted detection limit and is not a claim that none exists.

GLOBAL FALSIFIER of the angle's premise: either F3 or F5 alone answers "is there SAE-missed in-context structure beyond the top 64?" with no or largely no.

RESOURCE STOPS (e64 D1 guard): swap > 16 GB at any stage start; folder > 18 GB (delete caches first, then stop); system free disk < 8 GB -> abort. A partial output is deleted and re-run once (e65 section 13), and the re-run is reported. Every phase needs the user's go-ahead.
designs.compute_disk_estimate:
EXTRACTION (MPS). Raw L12 only, with no SAE step: about 1.5-2 min per 1,000 seqs, judging from e60's 103-198 s for 3 layers plus the SAE. P3 + D3 + S3 + R3 = 7,000 seqs, about 12-15 min.

DISK. fp16 at L12 is 0.59 GB per 1,000 seqs: P3 0.59 GB; D3, S3 and R3 1.18 GB each.
- They are processed in sequence: P3 is deleted after the choice freeze, S3 after G2/G3, R3 after G4, and D3 after G5.
- D3's units are kept as an fp16 npz (406k x 384, about 0.31 GB) together with the maps and meta.
- Peak folder about 15 GB (now 12 GB; cap 20 GB; the volume has 32 GB free). Final folder about 12.6 GB.

RAM. D3's V is about 1.9 GB in float32, plus float64 column-block temporaries; ranks for 384 units about 1.25 GB.

CPU.
- One ICA-192 fit took 12 s on 101k D2 rows, so expect 0.5-1.5 min per fit on D3 (203k rows), with skew slower.
- That is 6 fits per representation, plus the ICA-64 reference: P3 with 3 settings and the planted curve, about 20-30 min; D3, S3 and R3, about 10 min each.
- Permutation null: 2 labels x 1,000 permutations, a few minutes.
- trf parse of D3 (510k tokens): about 20-30 min.

COVERAGE. SAE encodes of D3's 406k rows for 13 dictionaries, about 15-20 min on MPS.

BEHAVIOUR (about 9.2 s per 200-prompt pass, e65):
- B5: 1 unsteered + 99 (64-d bank) + 99 (block bank) + 4 rig anchor + 4 block anchor + 4 second control + 4 supervised anchor + 4 x N candidates (N about 10-25 after G2-G5) = 255-315 passes, about 40-50 min.
- B6: about 110-130 passes, 17-20 min.
- C3: about 105-115 passes, about 17 min.

TOTALS. About 1.7 h MPS and 1.5-2 h CPU, so about 4 h of wall time spread over about 11 user-approved phases: calibrate, freeze, control, label, seal-reading, shuffled, replicate, coverage, steer B5, steer B6, confirm C3.
designs.main_risks:
1. THE BLOCK IS ONLY PARTLY SAE-DARK. On D2, block units' scores are about 31% SAE error (median 0.313, max 0.35, none >= 0.5), against 17% for top-64 units, and block A's variance is 30% error. ICA is not preferentially finding dark structure here. Block A is honestly "the first block where the SAE starts to fail"; it is not a dark subspace. The coverage gate may well return COVERED or PARTIALLY COVERED for most candidates, as e67 did. PCs 257-512 (56% error) are the named follow-up, on spare range 10,000-12,999.

2. THE CONTROLS ARE SHADOWS. paren and quote are the low-variance part of variables that also live in the top 64. The instrument is validated for "state variables partly in the block", not for block-native ones; no native known variable was isolated by one unit on D2. The planted detection limit bounds what a null result excludes.

3. THE BLOCK ANCHOR MAY HAVE NO CAUSAL WEIGHT. Pushing the low-variance component of quote state may not beat random block directions. That would leave block A with no behavioural verdict, as L7 was left (paren failed at L12 even in the top 64). This is the single largest term in p_positive.

4. THIN CONTROL MARGINS AND CONSTANTS SET AFTER A LOOK. Quote cleared D2's would-be floor by 0.009. The 0.6 multiplier, the 0.65 clip, K_max 256, the 0.75 shadow threshold and the tail-diversity caps were set with D2 in view (disclosed); P3 is the first blind use.

5. BOUNDARY AND BASIS INSTABILITY. lambda64/lambda65 differ by 1.8%, about 3 sampling SEs at about 68k PCA rows, and lambda256 is about lambda257, so units near the edges can rotate between sets. Mapping R3 and S3 through D3's maps, the boundary-band diagnostic and the R3 principal-angle report mitigate this but do not remove it. Only 43% of D2 units passed repro >= 0.8 on a single half.

6. LOCAL-CONTEXT VARIABLES DOMINATE. On D2 the battery names 64/192 units, mostly after_digit and next_* features; e64c's post hoc rules later named 9 v2 candidates. Survivors may again be previous- or next-token variables, nameable after the fact.

7. IDENTITY LEAKAGE. KIR 19.2 in the block without the per-type step, and per-type whitening in 192 dims is untested at scale.

8. LOAD AND MULTIPLICITY. 384 units; a reading load of perhaps 60-100 units; one analyst throughout (as in e64/e65).

9. THE SITES ARE CORPUS ROWS, NOT A FRESH RESERVE. Their only prior use was Stage-1 averaging. Truly fresh FineWeb would need network streaming, which is not in this plan.
designs.p_positive_finding:
About 0.04 (90% range 0.01-0.10) for the top class: a C3-confirmed, NOT COVERED, unnamed beyond-top-64 variable.

The chain:
- (a) Controls pass on P3 and D3: about 0.75. On D2, paren's single unit reached 0.720 against a would-be floor of 0.668, quote cleared by only 0.009, and D3's doubled rows may help.
- (b) The S3 yield gate passes: about 0.7. v2 at L12 had 51 against 27, but low-variance directions may carry formatting structure that survives shuffling.
- (c) The block anchor passes on B5: about 0.45. This is unknown territory: e65's L12 paren anchor failed even in the top 64.
- (d) Given (a)-(c), at least one family survives naming, S3, R3 and coverage (NOT COVERED) and passes B5 + B6: about 0.35. In v2, 2 of 31 L12 candidates passed B3 + B4 and one was top class; it was later COVERED. Block units are about 31% SAE error, so a single covering latent is somewhat less likely (P(not covered) about 0.45).
- (e) C3 confirms: about 0.7 (e66 confirmed both members).
- (f) It survives the post hoc naming checks: about 0.7.

Product: 0.75 x 0.7 x 0.45 x 0.35 x 0.7 x 0.7 = about 0.041.

CONDITIONAL FIGURE FOR WHEN THE BLOCK ANCHOR FAILS (no behavioural verdict possible). The design still yields a "replicated, uncovered, unnamed geometric lead" with probability about 0.12-0.15: (a) x (b) x P(at least one candidate replicates on R3, about 0.8, given v2's 17/31) x P(NOT COVERED, about 0.45) x P(unnamed after rules, about 0.6) = about 0.11-0.14.

The most likely single outcome, at about 0.3, is that controls and S3 pass, candidates replicate, and coverage returns COVERED or PARTIALLY COVERED: "largely no" again, but now for the block beyond PC 64.

designs.title: Skeptic-minimal SAE-gap pilot at L12: the identity-removed v2 pipeline on the SAE reconstruction error h − SAE(h). Calibration runs free on D2's stored raw rows; go/no-go in under an hour, before any larger prereg is written.
designs.layers:
L12 only. There are three reasons.

1. The e65 steering rig is validated only at L12. The L7 paren anchor failed in both e64 and e65.
2. results/e67_raw_L12_rows.npy holds the exact raw L12 residual on D2's 203,328 kept rows, aligned with occ_units_v2_L12.npz['row']. A read-only check today found no non-finite values. Coordinate 1038 peaks at 63,232; the next largest are 1125 at 2,256 and 412 at 1,296; the median per-coordinate max is 141.5. The model runs in bf16 (e65 §2). bf16's 8 significant bits sit inside fp16's 11 across fp16's normal range, and 63,232 < 65,504, so this fp16 file is lossless. Calibration therefore needs no extraction.
3. L14 overflows fp16 (67,072). L24's probe ceiling is below the 0.70 floor.

L7 is only a conditional follow-up arm, considered after an L12 GO. It would have no behavioural tier.
designs.representation:
One dictionary: the Gemma Scope 2 resid_post_all L12 16k l0_big JumpReLU SAE, encoded in fp32. All three arms come from the same raw rows h.

**Arms**
- **D (reference, not a gap arm).** fp16(z) @ W_dec, exactly as e60 builds it. It is used for P0 and as the comparator.
- **E (primary gap arm).** E = h − fp16(z) @ W_dec − b_dec, so H = D + E + b_dec exactly. b_dec cancels under mean removal but is kept so that "error" means the error. E holds two things: the sub-threshold drive that JumpReLU discards, and whatever the dictionary does not represent.
- **H (sanity arm).** Raw h. The natural control must be recovered here, because H contains D. H units count as gap units only if they pass the same G1–G3 screens.

**Not run: decoded beyond PCA-64.** It stays in the decoder span by construction, and e67 showed that span directions are blends of latents, so COVERED is the expected outcome. Truncation is tested inside E instead, by the spike-in, which can move k from 64 to 128.

**Recipe: the frozen v2 recipe, unchanged**
1. Rows: positions ≥ 4, types with ≥ 8 rows.
2. Dropped coordinates: e61.drop_for(12) = {1038} in every arm. In E only, also any coordinate whose calibration RMS is more than 20× the median coordinate RMS. This set is computed once on calibration before any ICA and then frozen.
3. Type, document and position means are removed, and the cycle is repeated 3 times.
4. PCA-k, whitened. k = 64 by default; k = 128 only if the spike rule requires it.
5. Per-type equalisation with N_MIN 32 and n0 16, then global re-whitening.

**Identity diagnostics:** self-excluded TDI at K = 128, and KIR. If KIR(E) > 20, one retune is allowed on calibration over e63's grid (N_MIN {32, 64, 128} × n0 {16, 64, 256}). It picks the lowest TDI under a guard of the control probe − 0.02, or the spike κ = 1 AUROC − 0.02 if there is no control.

**New extractions** (S-cal, D3, S3, R3) store only raw L12 h:
- fp16 if max|x| < 65,504 is asserted on every batch;
- otherwise fp32 for that block.

D, E and the pre-activations are recomputed on CPU from h, which is deterministic.
designs.positive_control:
Chosen on calibration (D2) only. This is tuning, and it is declared as such, the same way v2 tuned paren on P2.

**1. Probes.** A held-out probe (even/odd sequences, e63.probe) is fitted on E-W, D-W and H-W (k = 64) for:
- every binary extended-battery feature with ≥ 50 positives: paren, bracket, quote, squote_curly, enclosure, after_newline, list_item, after_colon, in_url, next_punct, and the rest;
- e67's label "next token is a preposition, subordinator or temporal word".

**2. Qualification.** A feature qualifies as E's natural control iff its E-probe is ≥ 0.72.
- Why 0.72: the frozen floor clip(0.5 + 0.75·(p − 0.5), 0.70, 0.85) is 0.70 for any p < 0.767. A lower qualifier would put the floor above the probe ceiling, which is v1's L24 failure.
- The margin is thin. At p = 0.72, a unit carrying 90–97% of the probe's excess (v2's range) lands at about 0.70–0.71. The prereg must say so, as REPORT flagged L12's P2 margin.
- Among qualifiers, the **tuned control** is the one with the largest (E-probe − D-probe) advantage. Above +0.03 it is an "SAE-gap control"; the advantage is reported either way. Using the advantage as a ranking rather than a requirement avoids leaving the branch with no qualifier.
- The **untuned control** is the next qualifier. It plays quote's role from v2 and is never used in any choice.

**3. Recovery.** The max screened |AUROC| (logcosh or skew ICA) must be ≥ the floor and above the p99.9 of the token-matched permutation null (1,000 permutations, seed 99, e63.null_engine). The **controlled branch** applies iff the tuned control is recovered in E.

**4. H must recover paren or quote** under the frozen v2 rule on calibration (D does, at 0.736 and 0.747). If H fails, that is a pipeline bug (STOP-P0).

**5. The spike-in always runs** (see control_fallback). It gives d_min, the size of variable that a negative result rules out.

**What to expect.** JumpReLU sends every latent's sub-threshold drive into E. Paren or quote state may therefore leak into E. That makes a covered control, which is fine for measuring sensitivity. E may also carry none, and then the fallback applies.
designs.control_fallback:
The **uncontrolled branch** applies when no feature reaches E-probe ≥ 0.72, or when the tuned control is not recovered by ICA on calibration.

**(a) Spike-in sensitivity control.** A planted synthetic variable, guaranteed absent from E.
- Spans: in each calibration sequence, random spans are placed uniformly until the base rate is 6.0% (calibration's quote rate). Their lengths are drawn from calibration's empirical quote_inside run lengths. Draw seeds 7101 and 7102.
- Planted direction: v = normalised N(0, I) over the kept coordinates, seeds 7201 and 7202.
- Planting, before identity removal: E_i ← E_i + κ·d_ref·σ_v·s_i·v, where:
  - σ_v = the SD of E·v after first-moment removal;
  - d_ref = the standardised mean difference of the frozen D L12 logcosh #33 score between quote_inside and not, on calibration;
  - κ ∈ {1, 0.5, 0.25}.
- Recovered iff some screened unit has |AUROC(y, s)| ≥ 0.70 and exceeds the p99 of the max screened |AUROC| over 100 unplanted span draws scored on the unspiked fit.
- Rule: κ = 1 must be recovered in both draws at k = 64. Otherwise repeat at k = 128 (ICA-128). If it still fails, STOP-SENS.
- d_min = the smallest κ·d_ref recovered in both draws. It is reported with every negative.

**(b) Behaviour still runs.**
- The D-arm L12 logcosh #33 quote direction (e64 maps) anchors each block. It validates the dose rule, the readout, SIG and sign consistency.
- The RAND bank built in E's own subspace is a null, so it needs no validation.
- Every pass in this branch is capped at **"exploratory, no in-arm natural control"** and is never called a discovery.
- **Asymmetry:** here a behavioural negative is not a falsifier. It cannot separate "no effect" from "rig blind to E-pullback directions at their own σ_d". Only a positive carries information.

**(c) A stricter GO bar:** the natural-to-shuffled gap-yield ratio must be ≥ 2.0×, against 1.5× in the controlled branch.
designs.data_splits:
**Calibration (the pilot):**
- **Cal = D2,** corpus 1,000–1,999, natural. L12 raw comes from results/e67_raw_L12_rows.npy and tokens from cache/occ/occD2_meta.npz. This is a seen set (labels, units and contexts were read), so it is used for calibration only and never as the discovery set.
- **S-cal** = the same 1,000 sequences, shuffled with e60's rule (seed 600,000 + seq_start + i). Its tokens are asserted equal to cache/occ/occS2_meta.npz. It needs one L12 raw extraction.

**After GO and a hashed PREREG_gap (none of these is extracted before):**

| block | content | role |
|---|---|---|
| D3 | corpus 2,000–2,999, natural | units, screens, control re-test, gap screens, labels |
| S3 | corpus 2,000–2,999, shuffled | context-shuffled null |
| R3 | corpus 3,000–3,999, natural | replication |
| B5 | corpus 4,000–4,999 | behaviour, test block |
| B6 | corpus 5,000–5,999 | behaviour, held-out |
| C | corpus 6,000–6,999 | one pre-named confirmatory test, in a separate confirm prereg frozen before C is touched |

**Behavioural sites.** 200 distinct sequences per block. One site per sequence, uniform in [5, 255] of the BOS-prepended 256-token row. The prompt is BOS + up to 64 preceding tokens + the site token: e65's rule, adapted to the 255-wide corpus rows.

**Untouched:** corpus 7,000–12,999 and 15,000–15,695, kept for an L7 arm or a second confirmation.

**Disclosures:**
- Every corpus range here was averaged into the Stage-1 type means. There is no Stage-4 selection link.
- Seeds are in a new 7000 series so nothing collides with the e64/e65 RNG streams: spike 7101–7202, sites 7500 + L, RAND 7510 + L, signature random sets 7400 + L.
designs.units_and_screens:
**Units**
- FastICA-k (k = 64, or 128 if the spike rule chose it), logcosh and skew, full rank.
- Fitted on every second row. Seed 0 for the main fit; seeds 1 and 2 for the even- and odd-sequence halves; retries at s + 100 and s + 200.
- No clusters: they were validated nowhere in v2, and the K = 16 partitions did not reproduce.

**Frozen v2 screens:** η²(token) of y ≤ 0.30; η²(token) of y² ≤ 0.30; split-half |cos| ≥ 0.8; bimodality off.

**New gap screens** (blind and label-free, computed before any label)

**G1, decoded-distinct.** Each unit is pulled back to 1152-d (pattern direction U_pca·diag(sd)·Cov(Z, ỹ_u), as e64 §8.2). Its max |cos| with all 128 frozen D L12 unit directions (e64_maps_L12.npz) must be < 0.8.

**G2, not decoded-predictable.** R²_D ≤ 0.49, where R²_D comes from a 2-fold (even/odd sequence) ridge regression (α = 1) of y_u on the D arm. That D arm is built with the same recipe at PCA-256, per-type whitened, on the same rows. The 0.49 is e67's |r| 0.7 bar, squared.

**G3, not SAE leakage.** R²_SAE ≤ 0.49.
- Take the 32 latents of the L12 16k big SAE with the largest |corr| between y_u and any of: a_j (the activation), pre_j, and s_j = clip(pre_j, 0, θ_j), the sub-threshold drive.
- These latents are selected on even sequences.
- Ridge-regress y_u on the 64 type-demeaned regressors {a_j, s_j}; take R² on odd sequences.
- The max single |r| with pre_j is also reported.

**Calibration of G2 and G3 (a P0 assertion; about 1 minute)**
- On calibration, G3 must **fail** six frozen units: the known-covered blend #13 and #16 (e67 showed it needs 11–62 atoms for cos 0.9, with a best single-latent r of only 0.40) and the four L12 control units (logcosh #11, #33; skew #23, #33).
- G2 must give R²_D ≥ 0.9 on all frozen D units.
- If G3 passes any of the six, the latent budget is raised to 64 and then to 128, in that order. The smallest budget that fails all six is frozen. If none does, STOP-G3.

**Definitions.** Gap unit = screened ∧ G1 ∧ G2 ∧ G3. Family = logcosh/skew twins at |cos| ≥ 0.8.

**Labelling** (D3, after freeze, before S3, R3 or behaviour), in order:
1. e64 §6.1's battery route on the extended battery (|AUROC| ≥ 0.75, or tail enrichment ≥ 3× and ≥ 0.10; |ρ| ≥ 0.5 for graded features).
2. e64c's 16 mechanical rules (en_core_web_trf 3.8.0): |AUROC| ≥ 0.65 names the unit.
3. A sealed 12-context reading per tail under §6.2's 8-of-12 standard.

**Candidate** = gap unit ∧ battery-UNNAMED ∧ not named by a rule ∧ not named by context.

**Identity.** tail-TDI and top-type share are reported. An identity-suspect unit (tail-TDI > 3 or share > 0.30) cannot reach the top class.
designs.nulls_and_gates:
**Pilot gates, on calibration, in order.** Each failure stops that arm.

**P0, instrument identity.** All of these must hold:
- D recomputed from the stored raw rows reproduces every frozen L12 Y_logcosh and Y_skew column as a linear readout of the recomputed W, with R² ≥ 0.9999 (e64's reconstruct got 1 − 4·10⁻¹⁴);
- S-cal tokens equal occS2_meta;
- the G2 and G3 calibration assertions pass.

**P1, identity removal in E.** KIR(E-W) ≤ 30 (D's is 9.3) and median K = 128 TDI ≤ 3.

**P2, sensitivity.** Spike κ = 1 recovered in both draws.

**P3, control.** The branch is assigned (controlled or uncontrolled), and H recovers paren or quote.

**P4, gap yield against the context-shuffled null.**
- N_gap(cal) and N_gap(S-cal) are counted like-for-like: each set gets its own representation, units, screens and G1–G3, and is battery-UNNAMED under the extended battery computed on its own tokens (as e64 did for S2).
- **GO iff all three hold:**
  - N_gap(cal) ≥ 3 units in ≥ 2 families;
  - N_gap(cal) ≥ ρ·N_gap(S-cal) + 1, with ρ = 1.5 in the controlled branch and 2.0 in the uncontrolled branch;
  - at least one gap unit is absent from S-cal, i.e. no S-cal unit refit in calibration's coordinates reaches |cos| ≥ 0.8 (e64's presence rule).
- **Reference:** the same contrast for the D arm on the same two sets. e64 saw 51 against 27 battery-UNNAMED units at L12.
- **Also reported:** the leak share, the fraction of screened E units failing G2 or G3.

**Full-prereg gates**
- **Control.** Re-tested on D3 with its frozen floor and a fresh 1,000-permutation token-matched null (p99.9), or with spike κ = 1 under fresh seeds in the uncontrolled branch. If it fails, STOP before any label is computed.
- **Shuffled null.** A candidate present in S3 (|cos| ≥ 0.8 in D3's coordinates) is disqualified as text-generic or an SAE artefact. The yield ratio is reported against the pilot's.
- **Replication on R3.** A candidate replicates iff:
  - an R3 unit, expressed in D3's coordinates, matches it at |cos| ≥ 0.8;
  - the screens and G1–G3 hold on R3;
  - it is still battery-UNNAMED on R3.
  - Chance is the p99.9 of the best |cos| over 1,000 random unit vectors (about 0.50 in v2).
- **Behaviour.** See behavioural_tier. The false-pass bound per unit is ≤ 1/(n′ + 1); the layer excess rule is Σ 1/(n′ + 1).
designs.behavioural_tier:
e65's rig, with its frozen code imported. Unchanged from e65:
- **Dose:** c·σ_d with c ∈ {0.5, 1, 2, 4}, gate at c* = 2. σ_d comes from the unsteered block pass (positions ≥ 4, about 12,000 positions).
- **Intervention:** h ← h + c·σ_d·d at the site, at the output of decoder layer 12.
- **Readout:** lse(T_u) − lse(R_u), steered minus unsteered.
- **Sign consistency:** ≥ 0.8 at some c ≤ 2.

**Adaptations, stated explicitly**
1. **RAND is rebuilt.** 99 pullback-matched directions in E's own whitened PCA-k: U_pca^E·diag(sd^E)·g, embedded at the kept coordinates, each dosed by its own σ. e65's L12 bank is in D's coordinates and is not valid here.
2. **SIG** scores u's push with every other screened E unit's blind signature. The twin is excluded, T_u's tokens are removed, and each signature must keep ≥ 5 tokens.
3. **Signatures:** e64.signature on D3's heavy-tail 1%. R_u is frequency-matched, from rng 7400 + 12.
4. **Anchors run first on every block.** The D L12 logcosh #33 quote direction always anchors. In the controlled branch, E's natural-control unit is a second anchor and must also pass. If an anchor fails, there is no verdict on that block.

**Blocks**
- **B5:** every replicated candidate, under the layer excess rule.
- **B6:** the anchors plus the B5 passes.
- **C:** one pre-named primary, chosen by e66's rule (logcosh member first). The per-test bound is ≤ 1/(n′ + 1).

**Wording**
- In the uncontrolled branch, every pass is "exploratory", and a negative is uninformative rather than a falsifier.
- Caveat: an E direction pushed in h-space may carry D components, so σ_d mixes the two scales. The anchor validates the rig, not E's dose scale.
designs.coverage_check:
The e67 rubric, extended for the error arm. It runs on every C-confirmed candidate, and descriptively on every candidate that passed B5 and B6, using D3.

**Dictionaries:** only those already on disk.
- resid_post_all 16k big and small at L10, L11, L12, L13 and L14;
- resid_post L13: 65k big, and 16k and 65k medium.

The 262k dictionaries were deleted. Re-download them (about 2.4 GB each, one at a time, under the 20 GB cap) only if a candidate is NOT COVERED by everything on disk.

**Per dictionary:**
- the max decoder |cos| with the pulled-back direction;
- an isotropic null (1,000 unit vectors) and a subspace null rebuilt in E's pullback (1,000);
- signed and non-negative OMP atom counts for cos 0.8 and 0.9;
- the best |r| between the unit's D3 score and each latent's activation **and pre-activation**. The pre-activation is new: it catches sub-threshold leakage that activation |r| misses. Everything is in fp32 throughout, the lesson of e67b.

**Verdicts**

| verdict | requires |
|---|---|
| **COVERED** | one latent with decoder \|cos\| ≥ 0.7, activation \|r\| ≥ 0.7 or pre-activation \|r\| ≥ 0.7, that also passes the behavioural match: ≥ 30% of its 200 strongest D3 rows are followed by a token in the unit's signature class, and that share is ≥ 3× the base rate |
| **PARTIALLY COVERED** | ≤ 5 decoder rows reach cos 0.9 in some dictionary, **or** G3's R²_SAE, recomputed with that dictionary, is ≥ 0.49 |
| **NOT COVERED** | otherwise |

The supervised next-token-category probe's cosine is reported, as in e67. The rubric note is hashed before any comparison.
designs.falsifiers_and_stop_rules:
**Pilot stops.** Each stops the arm; if both E and H stop, the program stops and no larger prereg is written.

| stop | trigger | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| STOP-P0 | readout R² < 0.9999; S-cal tokens ≠ occS2; H fails to recover paren or quote; or the G2 assertion (R²_D ≥ 0.9 on frozen D units) fails | fix the code; no E statistic is looked at |
| STOP-G3 | G3 cannot fail the six known-covered L12 units even at a 128-latent budget | the gap screen is uncalibrated, so "uncovered" cannot be certified |
| STOP-ID | KIR(E) > 30 after the one allowed retune | identity cannot be removed from E with this recipe |
| STOP-SENS | spike κ = 1 not recovered at k = 64 or k = 128 | the arm is blind; no conclusion either way |
| **F1, STOP-LEAK** | ≥ 90% of screened E units fail G2 or G3 | "at L12 the SAE error is the SAE's own sub-threshold and shrinkage residue" |
| **F2, STOP-YIELD** (the main falsifier) | the P4 GO rule fails | "no recoverable in-context structure in the SAE gap at L12 at sensitivity d_min" |

**After GO (full prereg)**

| falsifier | trigger | consequence |
|---|---|---|
| F3 | the control or spike fails on D3 | stop before labels |
| F4 | zero candidate families replicate on R3 | stop; geometric negative |
| F5 | an anchor fails on B5 | no behavioural verdict; outcome is geometric only |
| F6 | no candidate passes B5 beyond the Σ bound, or none passes B6 | a falsifier in the controlled branch only; in the uncontrolled branch a negative is uninformative |
| F7 | the C-confirmed candidate is COVERED by any dictionary on disk | "covered, not new", the e67 outcome |
| F8 | named by the battery, an e64c rule or the context reading | "named, not new" |

A positive finding must survive all of them.

**Resource stops** (abort the stage):
- swap > 16 GB at any stage start;
- project folder > 18 GB;
- free disk < 8 GB;
- the pilot's hard wall-clock cap of 75 minutes. If it is exceeded, report what was computed; there is no partial GO.

designs.main_risks:
1. **Leakage dominance (most likely).** E's non-Gaussian structure is the sub-threshold drive of existing latents, so nearly every unit fails G3. The design detects this cheaply as F1, an informative negative.
2. **A blend that slips through G2 and G3.** A direction spread over many latents, like #13 at 11–62 atoms, could pass. This is mitigated by calibrating G3 on the known-covered units and by the multi-dictionary coverage tier, but neither is airtight.
3. **Identity may be heavier in E** (SAE error is norm- and token-correlated), and the recipe was tuned on D. One retune is allowed, then STOP-ID.
4. **No natural control in E.** The spike-in proves sensitivity only for a sparse, span-like variable along a random direction. Dense or graded E variables may be harder to find, so a negative rules out only variables of that kind at or above d_min. Findings in that branch are capped at exploratory.
5. **The yield statistic is noisy at small counts** (for example 3 against 1). It is a go/no-go filter, not a claim.
6. **Thin control margin.** At E-probe 0.72, the expected unit sits right at the 0.70 floor.
7. **Steering E directions in h-space.** σ_d mixes D components, so the dose scale is not the E scale. The D anchor validates the rig, not E's dose.
8. **Forking in the pilot:** two arms (E and H) and the choice of k. Only the arm or arms that GO enter the prereg, with k frozen.
9. **Data history.** D2 is a seen set, used for calibration only. The corpus ranges were averaged into the Stage-1 type means.
10. **Machine.** MPS swap reached 18.7 GB during e67. Shuffled text could push coordinate 1038 past 65,504 (hence the fp32 fallback). The 262k dictionaries are absent, so coverage may be incomplete unless one is re-downloaded.
designs.p_positive_finding:
Two different numbers.

**P(pilot GO for E or H) ≈ 0.30.** ICA will find screened units in E. GO also needs at least 3 units that survive the decoded and leakage screens (G1–G3) and exceed shuffled text by 1.5–2×. JumpReLU leakage and the known density of SAE error (Engels et al. 2024: most SAE error is linearly predictable from the input) make F1 or F2 the modal outcome.

**P(a confirmed, uncovered, unnamed variable) ≈ 0.03.** The chain:
- P(GO) 0.30;
- × P(control or sensitivity holds on D3 and ≥ 1 family replicates | GO) ≈ 0.6;
- × P(passes B5, B6 and C with the anchor validated | replicated) ≈ 0.35;
- × P(NOT COVERED by the multi-dictionary rubric | confirmed, already past G3) ≈ 0.6;
- × P(not nameable by the battery, rules or context) ≈ 0.6.

That product is about 0.023, rounded up to 0.03 for the chance that the gap holds denser, genuinely unrepresented syntactic state.

**Base rates behind this:**
- Every earlier stage ended negative.
- The decoded instrument's only confirmed family (1 of about 65 candidates) was COVERED.
- 4 of 23 replicated families became nameable after the fact.

The pilot's value is that it shows within about an hour whether the expensive tiers are worth running.

scores.critique:
Strengths:
- It is the only design whose instrument fits the strongest fact in the D2 calibration. The scratchpad err_struct.log shows that the identity-removed L12 l0_big error is nearly Gaussian: every PC has excess kurtosis <= 0.8, and ICA-64/128/256 finds 0-2 screened units, against 50-107 in the decoded channel. Second-order temporal blind source separation (AMUSE) is the principled response, because it can separate Gaussian sources by their persistence.
- The search space is 100% SAE error by construction, so it answers 'where SAEs fail' most directly.
- The claim limits are honest: there is no natural control, so the knockout and planted controls (C1/C2) bound every null; the C3 extraction-sanity gate catches bugs; the gate order is explicit.
- D2 is burned, and its numbers are framed as a blind PREDICTION for D3. The `calib` phase must reproduce them, which is good discipline.
- S3 uses two criteria, including keeping >= 50% of the lag-1 autocorrelation under shuffling. That correctly targets the main confound: windowed attention averaging produces persistence even from iid tokens.
- The coverage tier is adapted to error directions: activation-level code R^2, the DISTRIBUTED-COVERED class, and lenient-to-COVERED rules.

Weaknesses:
- The KO control re-injects the SAE's own sparse paren/quote latents. It validates only sparse, SAE-amplitude, persistent variables, which is not the dense slow class the units actually belong to. C2 plants inside the searched top-256 subspace (the easy case), and the full-rank blind spot is admitted.
- AMUSE's top eigenvalues (0.229/0.214/0.208/0.199) are nearly degenerate. Refit-and-match replication at |cos| >= 0.8 can fail from rotation alone, so F5 could fire spuriously.
- The behavioural tier is badly matched to slow Gaussian units. Their tails span about 200 types and 210 documents, so e64.signature will be thin or empty, and a single-site push of a persistent variable is weak. The 0.3 chain probability for steering looks high; I estimate about 0.1-0.15.
- Coordinate 1125 is kept and there is no single-coordinate screen.
- The calibration scripts sit in a scratchpad that 'may be deleted'. They must be copied into docs/ and hashed before freezing.
- The disk estimate assumes an 11 GB baseline. The folder is now 17 GB, so D3+S3+R3 (1.8 GB) plus a 2.4 GB 262k download breaks the 20 GB cap unless option 1's downloads are deleted first.
- The p of about 0.03 is plausible, but S3-clean at 0.35 is probably optimistic.

Strengths:
- It has the strongest instrument and control story of the four. A natural control is present in block A: the paren probe is 0.780, ICA-192 unit #146 reaches 0.720 with split-half 0.93, and quote reaches 0.659.
- Separate fresh P3 calibration, with a fixed-order fallback ladder.
- D3 is doubled to 2,000 sequences to support 192-d ICA.
- A TOP64-SHADOW screen with a self-test.
- A like-for-like S3 yield gate.
- R3 and S3 are mapped through D3's frozen maps, which avoids basis rotation at nearly degenerate block edges.
- A block-native behavioural anchor gates the verdict, with a supervised non-gating anchor and a dose-void rule.
- A sealed C3 confirmation block.
- An explicit hash chain that copies the feasibility record into docs/.

Weaknesses:
- Construct validity against the goal is poor. feas_summary.txt shows block-A unit scores are only 29-35% SAE error (none >= 0.5), and block variance is 30% error. The block is mostly SAE span. Yet the coverage rubric has no distributed (code-R^2) or sub-threshold class, so a blend direction like e67's #13 (11-62 atoms, best single-latent r 0.40) could be awarded NOT COVERED. That is exactly the costly false-'not covered' error that NOTE_coverage_census.md warns against. The top class therefore means 'uncovered by one latent', not 'where SAEs fail'.
- The control floor was relaxed after seeing D2: multiplier 0.6 and clip 0.65, against v2's 0.75 and 0.70. This is disclosed, but quote clears D2's would-be floor by only 0.009.
- It consumes 8,000 fresh corpus sequences (2,000-9,999).
- The script name e68_extract_raw.py collides with the existing scripts/e68_coverage_census.py.
- The peak-disk estimate (15 GB) assumes a 12 GB baseline; the folder is now 17 GB.
- About 11 approval phases.
- The p of about 0.04 is inflated by the lenient coverage rubric.

Strengths:
- The exact per-unit decomposition y = y_sae + y_err, with ES calibrated against RAND-ES p99.9 and required under two SAEs, is the cleanest operational definition of 'SAE fails' in the set.
- The natural Tier A control is present in the raw residual: probes 0.81-0.82, and D2 pilot units reach paren 0.80 and quote 0.747.
- Tier C plants in h and re-runs the SAE, so it checks that the SAE does not absorb the signal.
- Separate fresh calibration set C3 (12,000-12,999).
- Duplicate-sequence screen and single-coordinate screen.
- The most complete coverage rubric: SUB-THRESHOLD, DISTRIBUTED and WIDTH-COVERED.
- Crisp F1-F10.

Weaknesses:

verdicts.fatal_flaws:
skeptic_minimal is fatal: its sensitivity gate (P2/STOP-SENS) cannot be passed.
- The spike plants kappa*d_ref*sigma_v along a FULL-RANK random direction v, with kappa in {1, 0.5, 0.25} and d_ref about 1, at a 6% base rate.
- A random 1151-d direction keeps only about 64/1151 of its norm^2 in the top-64 PCs of E. Those PCs hold 17.5% of E's variance (err_struct.log).
- So the whitened separation in the searched space is d' ≈ 0.13*kappa*d_ref, about 0.13 at kappa = 1. That gives AUROC ≈ 0.53, against the 0.70 bar. At k = 128 the result is not materially better.
- The design_sae_error_draft.txt calibration agrees: a full-rank random u was lost at kappa <= 2 even at k = 256.
- So the E arm ends at STOP-SENS, which the design itself labels 'the arm is blind; no conclusion either way'.
- The H arm cannot produce gap units: raw top-64 has a maximum ES of 0.28, so G2 removes them.
- The pilot therefore cannot reach its own GO, and its most likely output is uninformative.

No other design has a fatal flaw. These are serious but not fatal:
- low_variance: its coverage rubric has no distributed or sub-threshold class, and block A is about 70% SAE span (unit scores are at most 35% error). 'NOT COVERED' can therefore be awarded to SAE-span blends, which is construct-invalid for 'where SAEs fail'. Its control floor was also relaxed after seeing D2.
- raw_residual: ICA is mismatched to a nearly Gaussian error subspace, but the K* rule (a) catches this at the C3 calibration stage, at high cost.
- sae_error: its behavioural tier is structurally weak for slow Gaussian units (diffuse tails, so thin signatures). It may be unable to produce a PASS, which caps power but not validity.

Shared, and not fatal for any design: every disk estimate assumes an 11-12 GB baseline. du shows 17 GB, because option 1's census downloads arrived after e67. Every design's peak would exceed the 20 GB cap unless about 5.5 GB of those downloads are deleted first.

scores.critique:
Of the four, only this design changes the instrument to fit what the SAE error actually looks like. err_struct.log (scratchpad, run with v2's per-type step N_MIN 32 / n0 16) shows:
- every error PC has excess kurtosis <= 0.8, against up to 100+ in the decoded channel;
- ICA on e gives 0-3 screened units with split-half median 0.18-0.35;
- lagged CCA is 0.43 at lag 1, against a 0.08 null.
Second-order temporal BSS (AMUSE) is therefore the right contrast, and a non-Gaussian one is the wrong one.

Controls. The knockout control (C1: 20 frozen paren/quote latents re-inserted into e) is a natural variable actually present in an error-derived representation at the SAE's own amplitude, and it passed at alpha 1 and 0.5 on D2. C2 and C3 are sensible. The fallback wording bounds every null by C1/C2. The design is single-layer and single-instrument. D2 sightings are filed as a blind prediction for D3, and the gate order is clean.

Weaknesses:
- (1) Sub-threshold drive is not a verdict class. JumpReLU puts each latent's sub-threshold drive into e by construction, yet coverage uses only thresholded sparse codes (ridge R^2, single-latent \|r\|) and decoder cos. A pre-activation / clip(pre, 0, theta) class (skeptic G3, raw SUB-THRESHOLD) is missing. This is the main confound for any error-space search and the biggest validity deduction.
- (2) C2 plants directly into e. It never tests whether the SAE would have absorbed the planted variable.
- (3) The e65 rig is a poor fit for slow Gaussian units. A single-site push is scored by a 1%-tail next-token signature, and the tails span about 200 types and 210 documents. The dose sigma_d is taken on the RAW residual along an error direction, so the push may be dominated by the decoded component. The sigma ratio is reported but does not gate.
- (4) S3 is the dominant risk (P about 0.35). Bag-of-recent-token persistence (shared earlier tokens represented at both t and t-tau) predicts context-generic slow units. The linear 128-d bag rule (R^2 <= 0.04) is a weak test of this.
- (5) Wording: 'h = SAE(h) + e exactly complements the v2 channel' is not literally true. e60 uses fp16 codes and no b_dec. The mismatch is tiny, but C3 is not exactly v2's representation.
- (6) Calibration provenance lives in a session scratchpad 'which may be deleted'. It should be copied to docs/ and hashed.
- (7) The disk budget assumes an 11 GB base. The folder is 17 GB now (hf_home 12 GB, including the unused L7 and L13 262k l0_medium at 2.3 GB each), so the 262k re-download would breach 20 GB unless those are deleted first.

The positive probability of about 0.03 is honest.

Strengths:
- The exact linear decomposition y_u = y_sae + y_err (b_dec cancels under demeaning), with ES calibrated against random directions in the same frame, is the cleanest way in the set to measure 'how much of this unit is SAE failure'.
- Tier C is the best power control proposed. It plants a Markov state into h, re-runs the SAE, and requires recovery by an error-dominant unit, so it tests SAE absorption directly.
- Tier A uses natural controls that are genuinely present in the raw residual.
- Coverage adds SUB-THRESHOLD, DISTRIBUTED and WIDTH classes.
- It runs ES under two SAEs, uses a fresh calibration set (12,000-12,999) and has a duplicate screen.

Core problem: the instrument is mismatched to the target. err_struct.log shows the error is Gaussian in every marginal, so the non-Gaussianity full-rank ICA latches onto comes from the SAE-span part. The design's own pilot agrees: only 11 of 283 reproducible K=1024 units are error-leaning, and the number reaching ES 0.6 is unmeasured. At K=1024 the random-direction ES median is 0.505, so 'error-dominant' at >= 0.6 sits barely above chance geometry. F1/F4 (no K*, or zero error-dominant units) is the likely outcome. That would be a clean negative, but a weak search.

Further problems:
- ICA-1024 halves did not converge at 400 iterations, and split-half median is 0.54.
- Per-type whitening in 1,024 dimensions with many types below K rows is untested.
- 20 units have eta^2(y^2) > 0.3.
- Tier A passes on quote by about 0.05 at the fixed floor and would fail the formula floor.

Feasibility:
- Two layers (L7 has no behavioural tier and a likely Tier A fail), four new scripts, and about 10-12 h of wall time.
- The disk peak of about 16.3 GB was computed on an 11 GB base. At today's 17 GB it is about 22 GB, over the cap, unless the L7 and L13 262k medium dictionaries are deleted.

Falsifiers are thorough (F1-F10), though the gate stack is complex enough to invite forking.

Validity is the strongest of the four:
- The natural controls are measurably present in block A: single ICA units at 0.720 (paren) and 0.659 (quote) on D2, with block probes at 0.78 and 0.74.
- R3 and S3 are mapped through D3's frozen PCA and whitening maps, which avoids refit rotation in a flat spectrum.
- It adds a tail-diversity screen, a shadow screen against the top-64 with a self-test, and a non-gating supervised block anchor that separates 'block has no causal weight' from 'ICA unit too weak'.
- It adds a dose-void rule, honest disclosure of the constants set after the D2 look, and a P3 ladder that stops before D3.

The problem is the goal. The block is only modestly SAE-dark: block units' scores are 29-35% SAE error, with none >= 0.5, and the block itself is 30% error. So this is 'v2 beyond PC 64', not a search where SAEs fail. Its own modal outcome (about 0.3) is COVERED or PARTIALLY COVERED.

Other weaknesses:
- The controls are shadows of top-64 variables.
- Quote clears its post-look floor by 0.009.
- It consumes 8,000 of the roughly 11,700 untouched corpus sequences (2,000-9,999). That collides with any follow-up error-space study unless more FineWeb is streamed.
- The disk peak was computed from a 12 GB base. At 17 GB it is about 20.5 GB.

The structure is sound: a cheap go/no-go pilot on burned D2 before any prereg, with explicit STOP codes.

Its G3 leakage screen is the single most rigorous coverage-style tool in the set. It regresses y_u on the activations and the sub-threshold drive s_j = clip(pre_j, 0, theta_j) of the top-32 latents, and is CALIBRATED to fail known-covered positives: #13/#16 and the four L12 control units. Adding pre-activation \|r\| to coverage is also right.

But the primary E arm runs v2's non-Gaussian ICA-64 with the per-type step on e. That exact configuration already ran read-only on D2 (err_struct.py uses type_whiten with N_MIN 32 / n0 16). It gave 0-3 screened units, split-half median about 0.3, and every PC with excess kurtosis <= 0.8. ICA-64 fails the knockout control at alpha 0.5, and a 4-sigma planted source is lost. The pilot is therefore largely pre-answered: STOP-YIELD or STOP-SENS.

The H arm cannot produce gap units at PCA-64 by construction. The maximum error-variance share of any top-64 direction is 0.28, so G2 kills it. The design does not say this.

Other problems:
- E uses e60's fp16 codes, which injects code-quantisation noise correlated with active latents.
- P0's R^2 >= 0.9999 reproduction of the frozen Y columns compares a CPU fp32 re-encode against e60's MPS encode. JumpReLU threshold flips at the margin could trigger STOP-P0 on a non-bug. It needs a code-disagreement tolerance.
- In the uncontrolled branch a behavioural negative is declared uninformative, which weakens the falsifiability of that tier.

(c) low_variance. It is mis-targeted for 'where SAEs fail': the block's maximum SAE-error share is 0.35, and no unit reaches 0.5.

(d) sae_error, the winner. As written, it has no sub-threshold / pre-activation coverage class, which is the modal confound for anything found in a JumpReLU error. Graft skeptic_minimal's calibrated G3 before freezing.

scores.critique:
Best match to 'where SAEs fail': the units sit in h - SAE(h) by construction. Switching the instrument away from ICA is backed by data. I checked scratchpad err_struct.json: ICA on e at k=64 gives 2 logcosh and 0 skew screened units, with split-half medians of 0.30 and 0.32. PC excess kurtosis is at most 0.8. Lagged CCA is 0.43 against a null of 0.076.

The controls are honest. There is no natural control; the knockout (KO) control gates at alpha=1 and the planted control is in-subspace. C3 is a sound extraction-sanity gate.

The `calib` phase reproduces every D2 number from stored rows with no extraction, which is a strong engineering property.

Time to the main falsifier is short. S3-generic, which the design itself puts at about 0.65, is reached after about 6 min of MPS extraction and about 15 min of CPU.

Problems:
- (1) The disk baseline is wrong. The folder is 16.83 GB now, not 11 GB. D3+S3+R3 brings it to 18.6 GB; one 262k download brings it to 21.0 GB. Under its own '>18 GB delete caches' rule the peak is 19.84 GB, a 0.16 GB margin, and two L12 262k downloads are planned. It also misses that resid_post L13 262k l0_medium (2.42 GB) is already on disk.
- (2) The rig anchor (#33) is scored against a RAND bank built in e's PCA-256. That is not e65's validated configuration (a decoded 64-d pullback bank), so an anchor PASS there certifies nothing.
- (3) The units are Gaussian with diffuse tails (about 200 types and 210 documents in the top 300 rows). Signatures are likely empty, so the behavioural tier will probably be uninformative.
- (4) The KO control is sparse and large, so it overstates sensitivity to dense, slow structure.
- (5) The naming battery lacks next-token entropy and log p. A slow, Gaussian, persistent error component is exactly what a predictability regime would look like.

Strengths:
- Cleanest stop-rule structure of the four. The P3 ladder ends in a STOP before D3. The S3 yield gate is quantitative (>= 1.25x and >= 5). The global falsifier is explicit.
- A natural control is actually present in the representation: paren unit #146 reaches 0.720 on D2.
- Mapping R3 and S3 through D3's frozen maps is a sensible defence against basis rotation.
- Cheap: ICA-192 takes about 12 s per fit, and coverage needs no 262k download.

FATAL AS WRITTEN: e68_extract_raw zeroes coordinate 1038 before storage, but the coverage tier and the per-unit SAE-error shares encode 'D3's stored raw rows' with the JumpReLU SAE. I tested this read-only on 4,000 D2 rows with the L12 16k big SAE:
- zeroing 1038 raises L0 from 110 to 4,594;
- active-set Jaccard is 0.02;
- FVU on the other coordinates goes from 0.19 to 220.
Every activation |r| and every 'SAE-dark' share would therefore be garbage. The activation route to COVERED could never fire, so the rubric drifts toward NOT COVERED. That is the anti-conservative error this goal cannot afford. The fix is trivial: an fp32 sidecar for 1038, as the other three designs already have.

Other issues:
- Block units are only about 31% SAE error (max 0.35), so this is 'where SAEs start to fail' at best. The modal outcome is COVERED or PARTIALLY COVERED.
- Several constants were set after a look at D2. Quote's margin is 0.009.
- The peak folder is about 19.5 GB on the real 16.83 GB baseline (it assumed 12 GB): legal, but with a 0.5 GB margin.
- The script prefix e68 collides with the existing scripts/e68_coverage_census.py.
- 11 approval phases add operational drag.

Strengths:
- Most feasible: under 1 h, +0.7 GB, a hard 75-min cap, and only one model pass (S-cal).
- Excellent engineering ideas: G3 is calibrated so that it must FAIL the known-covered #13/#16 and the four control units before it is trusted; there is a pre-activation |r| coverage class; P0 is an exact-reproduction gate; the full prereg is written only after a GO.

The weakness: the E arm runs v2's ICA-64 on the error, and existing calibration already shows that instrument is blind there. err_struct.json for l0_big at k=64 has 2 screened logcosh units and 0 skew, with split-half medians of 0.30 and 0.32. A planted full-rank direction is lost at kappa <= 2 even at k=256. So GO, which needs >= 3 gap units in >= 2 families, is near-impossible, and the likely terminal state is STOP-SENS or STOP-YIELD: 'no conclusion either way'. That is an hour spent learning nothing new about e's content.

Other issues:
- The H arm at k=64 cannot produce error-resident units; the max error share in the top 64 is 0.28, so it adds little.
- It has the same single-RAND-bank anchor problem as sae_error: the #33 anchor is scored against an E-subspace bank.
- It says the 262k dictionaries are gone, but L13 resid_post 262k medium is on disk.
- If a 262k download is needed later, the full prereg reaches about 21 GB.

Its gating structure should be grafted onto the winner; it should not be run as-is.

Strengths:
- The exact linear split y_u = y_sae + y_err under the frozen maps is the most rigorous answer to 'how much of this unit lives in the error'.
- Measuring ES against the RAND-ES p99.9 is correct.
- It is honest that Tier B will be empty.
- RAND-E plus a separate anchor bank is the right behavioural design.

What its own D2 pilot shows (raw_check4d_K1024.json):
- ICA-1024 unit ES has quantiles 0.39/0.50/0.62/0.65 at p10/p50/p90/p99. Random directions have a median of 0.505 and a p99.9 of 0.539. The instrument shows no preference for error-resident structure, so 'error-dominant' is close to a chance label.
- Split-half median is 0.54. The paren control is not reproducible: screened paren is 0.537.
- Screened quote is 0.747, a 0.047 margin.
- Median excess kurtosis is 13 and eta2(y^2) reaches 0.76, a sign of identity or outlier leakage at K=1024.
- Only 11 of 283 reproducible units are error-leaning.

Feasibility is the worst of the four:
- two layers and four new scripts;
- a C3 grid of 3 K values x 10 whitening settings plus Tier C re-runs, at 1.5-2.5 h of CPU per layer, about 10+ h in all;
- on the real 16.83 GB baseline, D3+S3 (2.34 GB) plus two layers of K=1024 unit scores (1.66 GB) reach about 20.8 GB, and coverage with the 262k reaches about 21-22 GB, so the plan as written breaches the 20 GB cap;
- RAM: three fp32 arrays per layer plus ICA-1024 on a machine where e67 already reached 18.7 GB of swap.

The falsifiers are thorough (F1-F10), but the most likely outcome is a long run ending at F1 or F4.
